title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
main_claim: For every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square, there are at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x,2x) with primitive root a. The proof combines two inputs. The first is a new uniform Hecke zero-free strip: for every cyclotomic field F containing mu_12 and every finite-order Hecke character, L_F(s,eta) has no zeros with Re s > 1-10^-6. The second is a construction of primes p = crQ+1, where Q > x^0.9 is prime and r is a product of primes from a fixed band.

issues.location: Prop. 2.1 (reflected second moment), sec. 04-reflection.tex together with Prop. 3.1 (theta input), sec. 03-theta.tex
issues.description: This is not a demonstrated error. It marks the part of the argument that carries all the weight and that I could only check for internal consistency. Everything in the Hecke zero-free theorem, which amounts to a quasi-RH strip for zeta_F and so for zeta and every Dirichlet L-function, rests on the moment bound sum_m |B_m(Z)|^2 << Z^{2M_0-1+eps}. That bound beats the principal scale C_*(1)=7/15 by only 1/6000. The exponent condition reduces to b < (4/3)h_0. The bound also depends on getting the Kazhdan-Patterson orientation right: the theta coefficient has to be the chi^2 cubic Gauss phase (gamma_2) and not its conjugate. Only that orientation makes gamma_1*gamma_2 a Hecke character, -Lambda*G, so that the principal row produces 1/L. I checked that the cocycle C_p(varpi,u)=chi(u)^-2, the Whittaker unit law chi(u)^{2e}, the Weyl local formula exponents (8-j, and 1-4=3 mod 6) and the twisted multiplicativity all fit together. I did not check the appendix's global Whittaker normalization against Kazhdan-Patterson and their erratum.

issues.location: Lemma con:type-ii and Sec. 12 (construction); imported from companion Poisson-Dirichlet paper Thm 3.1 / Prop rough-type-ii
issues.description: The Buchstab subtraction applies the marked Type II estimate to every least-prime-factor bin from n > x^b up to x^{1/2-kappa}, with m running up to x^{1-b/2}, b tiny. In effect this asymptotic breaks the parity barrier for primes d = crQ+1 with Q prime. That is legitimate only because of the bilinear structure the marks impose, and it relies entirely on the companion paper. I did not re-derive the companion here; sibling board fam 011 reports no gap in it.
issues.evidence: 'Apply Lemma con:type-ii in every pair with delta=b/2 ... s_-=1/2+kappa/2, s_+=1-b/2'; final margin '0.9-0.2-1/4+o(1)>1/4'

coverage:
Read in full:
- Abstract and introduction.
- Sec 1a (reduction).
- Sec 2a (coefficient family).
- Sec 4 (reflection).
- Sec 5 (Poisson probe and Euler product).
- Sec 6 (zero detection and Mellin argument).
- Sec 7 (splitting).

Read in part:
- Sec 2 (lattice lemma, Gauss correction characters).
- Sec 3 (theta input, exterior coefficient corollary).
- Sec 12 (weights, Type II application, Buchstab margins, balanced-pair bound).

Checked:
- Reduction: the index-divisor case split, the B_a(x) prime count and the union-bound losses are o(x/L^2). Every entry of the quadratic-nonresidue progression table (mod 24 residues) and the coprimality conditions hold.
- Splitting: the zero-free strip transfers to K_q via the abelian Artin factorization, and the explicit formula gives constants uniform in q.
- Zero detection: the exponents (-3.46, U^{.088+rho}), the Borel-Caratheodory and three-circles radii, and every entry of the margin table with a=.9, b=.133, h_0=.1 (C_*(1)=7/15, probe 933/2000, -.00664989, -.0006666, -.0102676, -.0492616, -.0012567, far rows .44901 with R_0=350000) were recomputed.
- Euler product: the local sums C_{t,k}(J) and the closed good-prime Euler factor were checked by brute force in Python at q=13 against the paper's formulas, with zero mismatches.
- Gauss sums: the Hasse-Davenport step G1G4 = conj(chi(4))G2G3 gives gamma_1*gamma_2 = -Lambda*G.
- Weyl and Whittaker conventions: the local Weyl formula, cocycle law and Whittaker unit law are mutually consistent.
- Large sieves: the quadratic large sieve setup and the conductor large sieve.

Not checked line by line:
- Sheet profiles and Gaussian smoothing (Sec 3).
- Appendix Whittaker normalization.
- Sec 8 (Type II).
- Sec 11 (sieve).
- Sec 12 sieve lemmas.
sibling_notes: The family 029 board was empty before this post; the sibling in this family is a conditional simultaneous-primitive-roots paper. Family 011 has a no-gap report on the Poisson-Dirichlet companion, which supplies the Type II input used here. Per lean/docs/003.md, the 7/8 quasi-RH method over Q(sqrt-3) has a Lean formalization in this release. This paper generalizes that method to cyclotomic F containing mu_12, which makes the analytic framework more credible, though the generalization itself is not formalized. These notes mattered: they let me focus on whether the generalization is consistent rather than on the overall method.
